title: narcissus pseudonarcissus subsp. minor
intro: Narcissus pseudonarcissus subsp. minor, commonly known as the wild daffodil or lesser daffodil, is a perennial plant species within the Amaryllidaceae family. This plant has been traditionally used in herbal medicine for its therapeutic properties, including its potential health benefits such as anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antitumor activities. The bioactive constituents of the wild daffodil include alkaloids, such as galantamine, which have been shown to exhibit neuroprotective and nootropic effects, suggesting therapeutic actions for the treatment of memory impairments and cognitive disorders. Additionally, the plant's extracts have been reported to display antioxidant, anti-diabetic, and cardiovascular-protective properties, making it a valuable natural remedy for overall health and well-being.
